pointers.sentence: `FORMAT_SETTINGS` is the set of names that are formats (`django/utils/formats.py:FORMAT_SETTINGS`).
Each is also a setting, with a default (`django/conf/global_settings.py`):
The JavaScript catalogue sends the browser the same formats ([The language views: `set_language` and `JavaScriptCatalog`](views.md)) (`django/views/i18n.py:get_formats`).
`get_format` takes a format's name, and optionally a language code and `use_l10n=False` (`django/utils/formats.py:get_format`).
Anything a format module defines can be reached by name, by the `date` filter's argument too; the documentation warns against putting anything sensitive in one (`docs/topics/i18n/formatting.txt`).
`iter_format_modules` yields a language's modules in the order they are asked (`django/utils/formats.py:iter_format_modules`).

It first asks `django.utils.translation.check_for_language`: with `USE_I18N` true, a language for which no locale path holds a `"django"` catalogue, its own or its language's, gets no module, and all its formats are the settings' (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:translation_catalog_exists`); with it false, every language passes (`django/utils/translation/trans_null.py:check_for_language`).

It first asks `django.utils.translation.check_for_language`: with `USE_I18N` true, a language for which no locale path holds a `"django"` catalogue, its own or its language's, gets no module, and all its formats are the settings' (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:translation_catalog_exists`); with it false, every language passes (`django/utils/translation/trans_null.py:check_for_language`).
`get_format_modules` gives the list for a language, the active one by default, and keeps it in `_format_modules_cache` (`django/utils/formats.py:get_format_modules`).

`reset_format_cache` empties both; its docstring says it is primarily for testing, and `localize_settings_changed` calls it when a test overrides a format setting or `USE_THOUSAND_SEPARATOR` ([Overriding settings](../startup/overrides.md)) (`django/test/signals.py:localize_settings_changed`).
`get_format_lazy` is `get_format` made lazy, for a value made at import (`django/utils/formats.py:get_format_lazy`).

`DateField.input_formats` and `TimeField.input_formats` are such values (`django/forms/fields.py:DateField`), made once and read in the active language at each parse, so one `DateField` took `"29-03-2026"` in Dutch and refused it in English ([The built-in form fields](../forms/field-types.md)).
`django.utils.formats.localize` sends a value to the writer for its type (`django/utils/formats.py:localize`).

`number_format` gives the language's `DECIMAL_SEPARATOR`, `NUMBER_GROUPING` and `THOUSAND_SEPARATOR` to `django.utils.numberformat.format`, which groups the digits of a localized value where `USE_THOUSAND_SEPARATOR` is true, and of any value where `force_grouping=True` asks, but never with a grouping of 0 (`django/utils/formats.py:number_format`) (`django/utils/numberformat.py:format`).

`number_format` gives the language's `DECIMAL_SEPARATOR`, `NUMBER_GROUPING` and `THOUSAND_SEPARATOR` to `django.utils.numberformat.format`, which groups the digits of a localized value where `USE_THOUSAND_SEPARATOR` is true, and of any value where `force_grouping=True` asks, but never with a grouping of 0 (`django/utils/formats.py:number_format`) (`django/utils/numberformat.py:format`).

A localized widget, and every date or time input, writes its value with `localize_input`: a number through `number_format`, a date or time by strftime in a date or time input's own format, else the first of the locale's input formats, `"29-03-2026 11:30:00"` in Dutch ([Widgets: `Widget` and its subclasses](../forms/widgets.md)) (`django/utils/formats.py:localize_input`).

For a date or a datetime it first calls `sanitize_strftime_format`, which, where the platform does not pad a year below 1000 to four digits (glibc's does not), rewrites `"%Y"` and its kin with explicit padding (CPython issue 13305) (`django/utils/formats.py:sanitize_strftime_format`).
A localized integer, float or decimal field reads a typed number through `sanitize_separators` (`django/utils/formats.py:sanitize_separators`).
